title: Target trial emulation with a grace period: clone, censor, weight
summary: A per-protocol risk difference between 'start within a grace period' and 'never start' from observational data, by cloning each patient into both strategies, censoring deviations and weighting for them.

sizing._why: An emulated trial's precision depends on the weights and the censoring pattern; simulation or a bootstrap of the whole procedure.

pinned_defaults: Time zero at eligibility for both strategies; clones censored when their data stop agreeing with their strategy (the never arm at starting, the grace arm at the end of the grace period without starting).

Censoring weights from a pooled logistic model of starting given current severity, fitted on patient-intervals eligible to start; the never arm by the cumulative 1 / (1 - P(start)), last-interval starters in the grace arm by 1 / P(start).
Risk by weighted discrete-time Kaplan-Meier over 10 intervals. No confidence interval: that needs a bootstrap of the whole procedure.
_python_not_applicable: Owner decision E3 (2026-09-23): target trial emulation is included with a truth check only. The entry is R only; harness/selfcontrolled_examples.test.py re-implements the procedure in numpy as an oracle and must reproduce r.R's output, and recovery is measured by running r.R on 100 fixtures.
_naive: Two naive analyses on the same data: patients who ever started against those who never did (immortal time; mean bias -0.020 over 100 seeds) and the clone-censor analysis without weights (confounded by severity; mean bias +0.044).
